title: IL HB3851: SCH CD-CYBER-BULLYING

obligations: Each school district, charter school, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school shall create, maintain, and implement a policy on bullying, filed with the State Board of Education, based on the State Board of Education's template and including the criteria in the definition of policy on bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).

The policy or implementing procedure shall include a process to investigate whether a reported act of bullying is within the permissible scope of the district's or school's jurisdiction and shall require that the district or school provide the victim with information regarding services available within the district and community, such as counseling, support services, and other programs (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
School personnel available for help with a bully or to make a report about bullying shall be made known to parents or legal guardians, students, and school personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).

Every 2 years, each school district, charter school, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school shall conduct a review and re-evaluation of its policy and make any necessary and appropriate revisions; no later than September 30 of the subject year, the policy must be filed with the State Board of Education after being updated (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).

Each school district, charter school, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school shall collect, maintain, and submit to the State Board of Education non-identifiable data regarding verified allegations of bullying, in an annual report due no later than August 15 of each year starting with the 2024-2025 school year through the 2030-2031 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).

The State Board of Education shall adopt rules for the submission of data that includes a record of each verified allegation of bullying and action taken, and whether the instance was based on actual or perceived characteristics identified in subsection (a), consistent with student privacy laws (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).

Upon request of a parent or legal guardian, the State Board of Education must provide non-identifiable data on the number of bullying allegations and incidents in a given year in the school district, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school to the requesting parent or legal guardian (Sec. 27-23.7(g)).
By January 1, 2024, the State Board of Education shall post on its Internet website a template for a model bullying prevention policy (Sec. 27-23.7(h)).

The policy on bullying must include procedures for promptly reporting bullying, including identifying and providing the school e-mail address and school telephone number for the staff person responsible for receiving reports and a procedure for anonymous reporting (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of policy on bullying item 3).

The policy must include procedures for informing parents or guardians of all students involved in an alleged incident of bullying within 24 hours after the school's administration is made aware of the students' involvement, and discussing availability of social work services, counseling, school psychological services, other interventions, and restorative measures (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 4).

The policy must include procedures for promptly investigating and addressing reports of bullying, including making all reasonable efforts to complete the investigation within 10 school days, involving appropriate school support personnel, notifying the principal or school administrator as soon as possible, and providing parents and guardians information about the investigation and an opportunity to meet (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 5).

The policy must include interventions that can be taken to address bullying, such as school social work services, restorative measures, social-emotional skill building, counseling, school psychological services, and community-based services (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 6).

The policy must include a statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying and the consequences and appropriate remedial actions for a person who engages in reprisal or retaliation (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 7).

The policy must include consequences and appropriate remedial actions for a person found to have falsely accused another of bullying as a means of retaliation or as a means of bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 8).
The policy must be based on engagement of a range of school stakeholders, including students and parents or guardians (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 9).

The policy must be posted on the school's publicly accessible Internet website, included in the student handbook, posted where other policies are posted, provided periodically throughout the school year to students and faculty, and distributed annually to parents, guardians, students, and school personnel, including new employees when hired (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 10).

The policy must contain a policy evaluation process to assess outcomes and effectiveness, including frequency of victimization, observations of safety, identification of areas where bullying occurs, types of bullying, and bystander intervention or participation; information developed must be made available on the Internet website or otherwise provided (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 11).
The policy must be consistent with the policies of the school board, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 12).

The policy must require all individual instances of bullying, as well as all threats, suggestions, or instances of self-harm determined to be the result of bullying, to be reported to the parents or legal guardians of those involved under the guidelines in item 4 (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 13).
prohibitions: Bullying on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, physical appearance, socioeconomic status, academic status, pregnancy, parenting status, homelessness, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, military status, sexual orientation, gender-related identity or expression, unfavorable discharge from military service, association with a person or group with one or more of the aforementioned actual or perceived characteristics, or any other distinguishing characteristic is prohibited in all school districts, charter schools, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools (Sec. 27-23.7(a)).

No student shall be subjected to bullying during any school-sponsored education program or activity; while in school, on school property, on school buses or other school vehicles, at designated school bus stops waiting for the school bus, or at school-sponsored or school-sanctioned events or activities; through the transmission of information from a school computer, a school computer network, or other similar electronic school equipment; or through the transmission of information from a computer accessed at a nonschool-related location, activity, function, or program or from the use of technology or an electronic device not owned, leased, or used by a school district or school if the bullying causes a substantial disruption to the educational process or orderly operation of a school (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(1)-(4)).
The required policy must include a statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of policy on bullying item 7).
reading.what_it_does: Amends the School Code bullying prevention provisions to expand the definition of cyber-bullying to include posting or distribution of unauthorized digital replicas beginning with the 2026-2027 school year. Requires school districts, charter schools, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools to create, maintain, implement, and periodically file bullying prevention policies with the State Board of Education. Also requires collection and submission of nonidentifiable bullying data and authorizes grants for anti-bullying programming.
key_definitions: Artificial intelligence: has the meaning given to that term in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

Bullying: includes cyber-bullying and means any severe or pervasive physical or verbal act or conduct, including communications made in writing or electronically, directed toward a student or students that has or can be reasonably predicted to have the effect of one or more of the following: placing the student or students in reasonable fear of harm to the student's or students' person or property; causing a substantially detrimental effect on the student's or students' physical or mental health; substantially interfering with the student's or students' academic performance; or substantially interfering with the student's or students' ability to participate in or benefit from the services, activities, or privileges provided by a school (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

Cyber-bullying: bullying through the use of technology or any electronic communication, including without limitation any transfer of signs, signals, writing, images, sounds, data, or intelligence of any nature transmitted in whole or in part by a wire, radio, electromagnetic system, photoelectronic system, or photooptical system, including without limitation electronic mail, Internet communications, instant messages, or facsimile communications. Includes creation of a webpage or weblog in which the creator assumes the identity of another person or knowing impersonation of another person as author of posted content or messages if it creates bullying effects. Also includes distribution by electronic means of a communication to more than one person or posting of material on an electronic medium that may be accessed by one or more persons if it creates bullying effects. Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, also includes posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means if it creates bullying effects (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
Digital replica: has the meaning given to that term in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

Policy on bullying: a bullying prevention policy that meets 13 criteria listed in the definition, including the bullying definition, statement that bullying is contrary to State law, reporting procedures, parent notification within 24 hours, investigation procedures, interventions, anti-reprisal statement, consequences for false accusations, stakeholder engagement, posting and distribution requirements, evaluation process, consistency with school policies, and reporting of self-harm (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
Restorative measures: a continuum of school-based alternatives to exclusionary discipline, such as suspensions and expulsions, that meet seven listed purposes (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

School personnel: persons employed by, on contract with, or who volunteer in a school district, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school, including administrators, teachers, school social workers, school counselors, school psychologists, school nurses, cafeteria workers, custodians, bus drivers, school resource officers, and security guards (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
Unauthorized digital replica: the use of a digital replica of an individual without the consent of the depicted individual (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
compliance_steps: Review the current bullying prevention policy and update it to include the full statutory definition of bullying and cyber-bullying, including unauthorized digital replicas beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, and ensure all 13 criteria in the definition of policy on bullying are met (Sec. 27-23.7(b) and (d)).
File the updated policy with the State Board of Education no later than September 30 of the subject year, and repeat every 2 years after review and re-evaluation (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
Implement procedures for prompt reporting, including anonymous reporting, and make school personnel available for help known to parents, students, and personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 3 and (d)).

Implement parent or guardian notification within 24 hours of the school's administration becoming aware of students' involvement in an alleged incident, and discuss available services (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 4).

Implement investigation procedures, including completing investigations within 10 school days, involving appropriate personnel, notifying the principal, and providing parents information and an opportunity to meet (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 5).

Include interventions, anti-reprisal statement, consequences for false accusations, stakeholder engagement, posting and distribution requirements, evaluation process, consistency, and self-harm reporting in the policy (Sec. 27-23.7(b) items 6-13).

Collect, maintain, and submit non-identifiable data on verified bullying allegations annually by August 15, starting with the 2024-2025 school year through the 2030-2031 school year, in accordance with State Board of Education rules (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).

Ensure the policy is posted on the school's publicly accessible Internet website, included in the student handbook, and distributed annually to parents, guardians, students, and school personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 10).

If deploying AI tools that could generate digital replicas of students, ensure that any posting or distribution of unauthorized digital replicas is treated as cyber-bullying and addressed under the policy (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of cyber-bullying and unauthorized digital replica).
who_it_applies_to: nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools
notable_exemptions: Nothing in this Section is intended to infringe upon any right to exercise free expression or the free exercise of religion or religiously based views protected under the First Amendment to the United States Constitution or under Section 3 of Article I of the Illinois Constitution (Sec. 27-23.7(a-5)).

The prohibition on bullying through transmission of information from a computer accessed at a nonschool-related location, activity, function, or program or from use of technology or electronic device not owned, leased, or used by a school applies only in cases in which a school administrator or teacher receives a report that bullying through this means has occurred and does not require a district or school to staff or monitor any nonschool-related activity, function, or program (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(4)).

What it does

Amends the School Code bullying prevention provisions to expand the definition of cyber-bullying to include posting or distribution of unauthorized digital replicas beginning with the 2026-2027 school year. Requires school districts, charter schools, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools to create, maintain, implement, and periodically file bullying prevention policies with the State Board of Education. Also requires collection and submission of nonidentifiable bullying data and authorizes grants for anti-bullying programming.

Who it applies to

  • school districts
  • charter schools
  • nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools

Effective date

July 1, 2026

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence: has the meaning given to that term in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
  • Bullying: includes cyber-bullying and means any severe or pervasive physical or verbal act or conduct, including communications made in writing or electronically, directed toward a student or students that has or can be reasonably predicted to have the effect of one or more of the following: placing the student or students in reasonable fear of harm to the student's or students' person or property; causing a substantially detrimental effect on the student's or students' physical or mental health; substantially interfering with the student's or students' academic performance; or substantially interfering with the student's or students' ability to participate in or benefit from the services, activities, or privileges provided by a school (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
  • Cyber-bullying: bullying through the use of technology or any electronic communication, including without limitation any transfer of signs, signals, writing, images, sounds, data, or intelligence of any nature transmitted in whole or in part by a wire, radio, electromagnetic system, photoelectronic system, or photooptical system, including without limitation electronic mail, Internet communications, instant messages, or facsimile communications. Includes creation of a webpage or weblog in which the creator assumes the identity of another person or knowing impersonation of another person as author of posted content or messages if it creates bullying effects. Also includes distribution by electronic means of a communication to more than one person or posting of material on an electronic medium that may be accessed by one or more persons if it creates bullying effects. Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, also includes posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means if it creates bullying effects (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
  • Digital replica: has the meaning given to that term in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
  • Policy on bullying: a bullying prevention policy that meets 13 criteria listed in the definition, including the bullying definition, statement that bullying is contrary to State law, reporting procedures, parent notification within 24 hours, investigation procedures, interventions, anti-reprisal statement, consequences for false accusations, stakeholder engagement, posting and distribution requirements, evaluation process, consistency with school policies, and reporting of self-harm (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
  • Restorative measures: a continuum of school-based alternatives to exclusionary discipline, such as suspensions and expulsions, that meet seven listed purposes (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
  • School personnel: persons employed by, on contract with, or who volunteer in a school district, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school, including administrators, teachers, school social workers, school counselors, school psychologists, school nurses, cafeteria workers, custodians, bus drivers, school resource officers, and security guards (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).
  • Unauthorized digital replica: the use of a digital replica of an individual without the consent of the depicted individual (Sec. 27-23.7(b)).

Obligations

  • Each school district, charter school, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school shall create, maintain, and implement a policy on bullying, filed with the State Board of Education, based on the State Board of Education's template and including the criteria in the definition of policy on bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • The policy or implementing procedure shall include a process to investigate whether a reported act of bullying is within the permissible scope of the district's or school's jurisdiction and shall require that the district or school provide the victim with information regarding services available within the district and community, such as counseling, support services, and other programs (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • School personnel available for help with a bully or to make a report about bullying shall be made known to parents or legal guardians, students, and school personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • Every 2 years, each school district, charter school, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school shall conduct a review and re-evaluation of its policy and make any necessary and appropriate revisions; no later than September 30 of the subject year, the policy must be filed with the State Board of Education after being updated (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • Each school district, charter school, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school shall collect, maintain, and submit to the State Board of Education non-identifiable data regarding verified allegations of bullying, in an annual report due no later than August 15 of each year starting with the 2024-2025 school year through the 2030-2031 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).
  • The State Board of Education shall adopt rules for the submission of data that includes a record of each verified allegation of bullying and action taken, and whether the instance was based on actual or perceived characteristics identified in subsection (a), consistent with student privacy laws (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).
  • Upon request of a parent or legal guardian, the State Board of Education must provide non-identifiable data on the number of bullying allegations and incidents in a given year in the school district, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school to the requesting parent or legal guardian (Sec. 27-23.7(g)).
  • By January 1, 2024, the State Board of Education shall post on its Internet website a template for a model bullying prevention policy (Sec. 27-23.7(h)).
  • The policy on bullying must include procedures for promptly reporting bullying, including identifying and providing the school e-mail address and school telephone number for the staff person responsible for receiving reports and a procedure for anonymous reporting (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of policy on bullying item 3).
  • The policy must include procedures for informing parents or guardians of all students involved in an alleged incident of bullying within 24 hours after the school's administration is made aware of the students' involvement, and discussing availability of social work services, counseling, school psychological services, other interventions, and restorative measures (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 4).
  • The policy must include procedures for promptly investigating and addressing reports of bullying, including making all reasonable efforts to complete the investigation within 10 school days, involving appropriate school support personnel, notifying the principal or school administrator as soon as possible, and providing parents and guardians information about the investigation and an opportunity to meet (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 5).
  • The policy must include interventions that can be taken to address bullying, such as school social work services, restorative measures, social-emotional skill building, counseling, school psychological services, and community-based services (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 6).
  • The policy must include a statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying and the consequences and appropriate remedial actions for a person who engages in reprisal or retaliation (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 7).
  • The policy must include consequences and appropriate remedial actions for a person found to have falsely accused another of bullying as a means of retaliation or as a means of bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 8).
  • The policy must be based on engagement of a range of school stakeholders, including students and parents or guardians (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 9).
  • The policy must be posted on the school's publicly accessible Internet website, included in the student handbook, posted where other policies are posted, provided periodically throughout the school year to students and faculty, and distributed annually to parents, guardians, students, and school personnel, including new employees when hired (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 10).
  • The policy must contain a policy evaluation process to assess outcomes and effectiveness, including frequency of victimization, observations of safety, identification of areas where bullying occurs, types of bullying, and bystander intervention or participation; information developed must be made available on the Internet website or otherwise provided (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 11).
  • The policy must be consistent with the policies of the school board, charter school, or nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary or secondary school (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 12).
  • The policy must require all individual instances of bullying, as well as all threats, suggestions, or instances of self-harm determined to be the result of bullying, to be reported to the parents or legal guardians of those involved under the guidelines in item 4 (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 13).

Prohibitions

  • Bullying on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, physical appearance, socioeconomic status, academic status, pregnancy, parenting status, homelessness, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, military status, sexual orientation, gender-related identity or expression, unfavorable discharge from military service, association with a person or group with one or more of the aforementioned actual or perceived characteristics, or any other distinguishing characteristic is prohibited in all school districts, charter schools, and nonpublic, nonsectarian elementary and secondary schools (Sec. 27-23.7(a)).
  • No student shall be subjected to bullying during any school-sponsored education program or activity; while in school, on school property, on school buses or other school vehicles, at designated school bus stops waiting for the school bus, or at school-sponsored or school-sanctioned events or activities; through the transmission of information from a school computer, a school computer network, or other similar electronic school equipment; or through the transmission of information from a computer accessed at a nonschool-related location, activity, function, or program or from the use of technology or an electronic device not owned, leased, or used by a school district or school if the bullying causes a substantial disruption to the educational process or orderly operation of a school (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(1)-(4)).
  • The required policy must include a statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of policy on bullying item 7).

Penalties and enforcement

The State Board of Education monitors and provides technical support for implementation of policies, reviews each filed policy to ensure it meets requirements, and if a school fails to file a policy by September 30, provides a written request for filing; if the school fails to file within 14 days of receipt, the State Board of Education publishes notice of non-compliance on its website (Sec. 27-23.7(d)). The State Board of Education adopts rules regarding notification of schools that fail to comply with data submission requirements (Sec. 27-23.7(f)). Schools not in compliance with subsection (f) are not eligible to receive a grant from the Illinois Bullying and Cyberbullying Prevention Fund (Sec. 27-23.7(j)). No monetary penalties or private right of action are created by this Section; subsection (e) states this Section shall not be interpreted to prevent a victim from seeking redress under any other available civil or criminal law (Sec. 27-23.7(e)).

How it affects AI deployment

  • Beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, cyber-bullying includes the posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means if it creates any of the effects enumerated in the definition of bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of cyber-bullying).
  • An unauthorized digital replica is the use of a digital replica of an individual without the consent of the depicted individual, and digital replica has the meaning given in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definitions of unauthorized digital replica and digital replica).
  • Schools must update their bullying prevention policies to include this expanded cyber-bullying definition and address reports involving AI-generated or synthetic media of students (Sec. 27-23.7(d) and (b) definition of policy on bullying).
  • Schools must investigate reported incidents involving unauthorized digital replicas under the same procedures, including parent notification within 24 hours and completion within 10 school days (Sec. 27-23.7(b) items 4 and 5).
  • Schools must collect and submit non-identifiable data on verified allegations of bullying, which would include incidents involving unauthorized digital replicas, in annual reports (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).
  • The statute defines artificial intelligence by reference to the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act but does not impose separate AI-specific obligations beyond the unauthorized digital replica provisions (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of artificial intelligence).

Notable exemptions

  • Nothing in this Section is intended to infringe upon any right to exercise free expression or the free exercise of religion or religiously based views protected under the First Amendment to the United States Constitution or under Section 3 of Article I of the Illinois Constitution (Sec. 27-23.7(a-5)).
  • The prohibition on bullying through transmission of information from a computer accessed at a nonschool-related location, activity, function, or program or from use of technology or electronic device not owned, leased, or used by a school applies only in cases in which a school administrator or teacher receives a report that bullying through this means has occurred and does not require a district or school to staff or monitor any nonschool-related activity, function, or program (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(4)).
  • This Section shall not be interpreted to prevent a victim from seeking redress under any other available civil or criminal law (Sec. 27-23.7(e)).
  • Formal disciplinary action cannot be taken solely on the basis of an anonymous report (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of policy on bullying item 3).

Compliance steps

  • Review the current bullying prevention policy and update it to include the full statutory definition of bullying and cyber-bullying, including unauthorized digital replicas beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, and ensure all 13 criteria in the definition of policy on bullying are met (Sec. 27-23.7(b) and (d)).
  • File the updated policy with the State Board of Education no later than September 30 of the subject year, and repeat every 2 years after review and re-evaluation (Sec. 27-23.7(d)).
  • Implement procedures for prompt reporting, including anonymous reporting, and make school personnel available for help known to parents, students, and personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 3 and (d)).
  • Implement parent or guardian notification within 24 hours of the school's administration becoming aware of students' involvement in an alleged incident, and discuss available services (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 4).
  • Implement investigation procedures, including completing investigations within 10 school days, involving appropriate personnel, notifying the principal, and providing parents information and an opportunity to meet (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 5).
  • Include interventions, anti-reprisal statement, consequences for false accusations, stakeholder engagement, posting and distribution requirements, evaluation process, consistency, and self-harm reporting in the policy (Sec. 27-23.7(b) items 6-13).
  • Collect, maintain, and submit non-identifiable data on verified bullying allegations annually by August 15, starting with the 2024-2025 school year through the 2030-2031 school year, in accordance with State Board of Education rules (Sec. 27-23.7(f)).
  • Ensure the policy is posted on the school's publicly accessible Internet website, included in the student handbook, and distributed annually to parents, guardians, students, and school personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(b) item 10).
  • If deploying AI tools that could generate digital replicas of students, ensure that any posting or distribution of unauthorized digital replicas is treated as cyber-bullying and addressed under the policy (Sec. 27-23.7(b) definition of cyber-bullying and unauthorized digital replica).
